_comment: U.S. state (plus DC) data-breach notification law reference. Seeded 2026-08-02 from statutory research with an independent adversarial cross-check pass (28 corrections applied). Fields prefixed with _ are research metadata, not loaded into D1. Each row must be re-verified against its official statute_url before the /rights/[state] page ships in Phase 3. Unconfirmable numbers are stored null, never guessed.

rows._notes: Alaska Personal Information Protection Act (Alaska Stat. §§ 45.48.010–.090). Individual notice 'in the most expeditious time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. No affirmative AG-notice duty for disclosed breaches; written AG notice required only when invoking the no-reasonable-likelihood-of-harm exception (§ 45.48.010(c)), so ag_report_threshold is null. Consumer reporting agencies must be notified if more than 1,000 residents affected (§ 45.48.040). URL is official akleg.gov BASIS statutes page anchored to the section.

Data Breach Notification Act of 2018 (Ala. Code §§ 8-38-1 to 8-38-12). Individual notice 'as expeditiously as possible and without unreasonable delay' but no later than 45 days after determination (§ 8-38-5). AG notice under § 8-38-6 when the number of individuals notified exceeds 1,000 (i.e. 1,001+, recorded as at/above value), within the same 45-day window. Verified against § 8-38-6 text ('exceeds 1,000'). ALISON Code of Alabama browser has no stable section-level deep link; URL is the official code landing page — navigate to Title 8, Chapter 38.

Personal Information Protection Act (Ark. Code Ann. §§ 4-110-101 to 4-110-108). Individual notice in 'the most expedient time and manner possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count for individuals. Act 1030 of 2019 (HB 1943) added AG notice when the breach affects more than 1,000 individuals (1,001+, recorded as at/above value), due at the same time as individual notice or within 45 days of the reasonable-likelihood-of-harm determination, whichever occurs first — that 45-day timing applies to AG notice only, not individual notice. Official Arkansas Code online is Lexis-hosted public access via the General Assembly site with no stable official section deep link; URL is the arkleg.state.ar.us gateway — flag for manual re-verification.

Relocated from former Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 44-7501 in 2018. Individual notice within 45 days of determination. If more than 1,000 individuals affected (1,001+, recorded as at/above value), must also notify the Attorney General, the Director of the Arizona Department of Homeland Security (added by HB 2146, 2022), and the three largest consumer reporting agencies within the same 45 days. URL verified as the official azleg.gov section page.

Individual notice 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. When a single breach requires notice to more than 500 California residents (501+, recorded as at/above value), a sample copy of the notification must be submitted electronically to the Attorney General. § 1798.82 covers businesses; parallel state-agency provision is Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.29. Credit monitoring/identity theft prevention is not mandated; if offered, it must run at least 12 months — hence mandated_monitoring_months is null. The leginfo URL's sectionNum parameter includes a trailing period as generated by the official site.

As amended by HB 18-1128 (effective Sept. 1, 2018): individual notice in the most expedient time possible but not later than 30 days after determination of a security breach — among the shortest fixed deadlines in the U.S. AG notice required when the breach is reasonably believed to have affected 500 or more Colorado residents (at/above value exactly 500), also within 30 days; excused if the investigation determines misuse has not occurred and is not reasonably likely. CRA notice at more than 1,000 residents. Official CRS published via a LexisNexis-hosted service with no stable section deep link; URL is the official CRS landing page on leg.colorado.gov — flag for manual re-verification.

As amended by Public Act 21-59 (effective Oct. 1, 2021), which shortened the deadline from 90 to 60 days after discovery and expanded 'personal information'. AG notice required for every breach requiring resident notification, not later than the time residents are notified — no numeric threshold, hence 1. When the breach involves Social Security or taxpayer identification numbers, at least 24 months of free identity theft prevention services (plus mitigation services if identity theft occurs) must be provided — raised from 12 to 24 months by PA 18-90 (2018). URL is the official cga.ct.gov chapter page anchored to the section.

As amended by the Security Breach Protection Amendment Act of 2020 (D.C. Law 23-98, effective June 2020). Individual notice 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. Written AG notice required when 50 or more District residents are affected (at/above value exactly 50, per § 28-3852(b-1)), no later than when residents are notified. When the breach involves Social Security or taxpayer identification numbers, at least 18 months of free identity theft protection services must be offered. URL is the official D.C. Law Library (Council of the District of Columbia).

As amended effective April 14, 2018. Individual notice without unreasonable delay but not later than 60 days after determination of the breach. AG notice required, not later than the time individual notice is provided, when the number of affected Delaware residents exceeds 500 (statutory text 'exceeds 500', i.e. 501+, recorded as at/above value — some secondary summaries loosely say '500 or more'; the statute says 'exceeds'). When SSNs are involved, the entity must offer at least 1 year (12 months) of free credit monitoring (§ 12B-102(e)). URL is the official delcode.delaware.gov chapter page containing § 12B-102.

Verified. Florida Information Protection Act (FIPA). Individual notice due as expeditiously as practicable but no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred; 15-day extension available for good cause shown in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs. Notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (the AG's department) required for breaches affecting 500 OR MORE individuals in Florida ('500 or more' — inclusive, so 500 is the correct at/above threshold), also within 30 days. URL is the Legislature's official Online Sunshine site; flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes also official.

Verified with one note correction. O.C.G.A. §§ 10-1-910 to 10-1-915. Narrow scope: applies to 'information brokers' (entities collecting personal information to furnish to third parties) and 'data collectors' — under § 10-1-911 a data collector is a STATE OR LOCAL GOVERNMENT agency/instrumentality itself (excluding records maintained primarily for traffic safety, law enforcement, licensing, etc.), not (as the original note said) private entities maintaining data on behalf of agencies; those third-party maintainers are covered separately by § 10-1-912(b). Notice 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. No AG/state-agency notice requirement; consumer reporting agencies must be notified if more than 10,000 Georgia residents are notified at one time. Official O.C.G.A. is published online by LexisNexis under state contract and does not support stable deep links — manual navigation to Title 10, Ch. 1, Art. 34 required.

Verified. Individual notice 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. Statutory text: a business that provides notice to MORE THAN one thousand persons at one time must notify in writing the State of Hawaii Office of Consumer Protection (not the AG per se) and nationwide consumer reporting agencies — hence 1001. Trigger is measured by persons notified at one time, not strictly by count of Hawaii residents affected (some secondary sources loosely paraphrase as '1,000 or more'; the statute says 'more than'). Government agencies have separate legislative reporting duties under § 487N-4. Capitol.hawaii.gov section-level URL paths occasionally change; verify link resolves.

Verified. Individual notice 'in the most expeditious manner possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. Written notice to the director of the AG's Consumer Protection Division required when a breach requires notification of MORE THAN five hundred Iowa residents (statutory text 'more than five hundred' — 501 is correct; AG-office summaries that say 'at least 500' are paraphrases), due within 5 business days after giving notice to any consumer. Definitions in Iowa Code § 715C.1. URL is the Iowa Legislature's official PDF of the section; an HTML browse view also exists at legis.iowa.gov.

Verified. Notice to individuals 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. No AG-notice requirement for private/commercial entities (threshold null on that basis). Exception: Idaho city, county, and state PUBLIC AGENCIES must notify the Attorney General within 24 hours of discovering a breach regardless of resident count — a time-based, entity-specific duty that does not fit the resident-count field. Definitions in Idaho Code § 28-51-104; penalties in § 28-51-107. URL is the official Idaho Legislature statutes site.

Verified with one note correction. Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). Individual notice 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. AG notice (added by P.A. 101-0343 / SB 1624, eff. 1/1/2020) required when a single breach requires notice to MORE THAN 500 Illinois residents — recorded as 501; CORRECTION vs. authored row: for private data collectors this AG notice is due 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, but in no event later than when the data collector provides notice to consumers' — there is NO 45-day clock in 530/10. The '45 days of discovery or when consumer notice is provided, whichever is sooner' rule belongs to STATE AGENCIES under 815 ILCS 530/12, triggered at more than 250 Illinois residents. PIPA also covers medical, biometric, and online-credential data (credential-only breaches allow email/online notice). URL updated to ILGA's current canonical scheme; the legacy ilcs3.asp URL redirects to it.

Verified. HEA 1351 / HB 1351 (2022, eff. 7/1/2022) added the fixed outer limit: notice without unreasonable delay but not more than 45 days after discovery (Ind. Code § 24-4.9-3-3), subject to statutory reasonable-delay grounds (system restoration, scoping, law-enforcement/AG request). Every breach requiring individual notice must also be disclosed to the Indiana Attorney General — no resident-count threshold, recorded as 1. Consumer reporting agencies must be notified when disclosure goes to more than 1,000 consumers. An unencrypted/unredacted SSN triggers notice even WITHOUT the individual's name (broader than most states). The iga.in.gov 'laws' URL is versioned by year with fragment anchors — re-verify the 2025 segment and #24-4.9-3-1 anchor against the current publication year.

Verified. Notice to affected Kansas residents 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' following a good-faith investigation finding misuse has occurred or is reasonably likely — no fixed day count. No AG/state-agency notice requirement in the general breach statute (threshold null); sector-specific regimes (e.g. insurance data security notice to the Insurance Commissioner) exist separately. Consumer reporting agencies must be notified when more than 1,000 consumers are notified at one time. Definitions in Kan. Stat. Ann. § 50-7a01. URL is the official Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes site (ksrevisor.gov; the older ksrevisor.org host serves the same content).

Private-sector statute: notice in 'most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count, hence null. No AG/agency notice requirement under KRS 365.732; CRA notice if >1,000 notified. A separate regime for public agencies and their contractors (KRS 61.931–61.934) DOES require notice to state officials incl. the AG and uses a 35-day framework — do not conflate. Triggers: name + SSN, driver's license, or account number w/ access code. Verification caveat: the statute-page URL format is correct for apps.legislature.ky.gov but the id=43326 parameter could not be fetched for confirmation — spot-check that it resolves to KRS 365.732.

rows.statute_citation: La. Rev. Stat. § 51:3074; La. Admin. Code tit. 16, pt. III, § 701
rows._notes: 60-day deadline from discovery (2018 Act 382) verified; AG may grant extension if written reasons provided within the 60-day window. AG notice threshold of 1 comes from La. Admin. Code tit. 16, pt. III, § 701 — written notice to the AG's Consumer Protection Section within 10 days of distributing notice to citizens, including names of affected LA citizens; late AG notice carries fines up to $5,000/violation. This is regulatory, not in the statute text — verified current as of Aug 2026 via AG office guidance and firm trackers. Personal information includes SSN and (post-2018) state ID, passport number, and biometric data. Database Security Breach Notification Law spans R.S. 51:3071–3077.

'As soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. Every covered breach must be reported to BOTH the AG and the Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation (threshold 1); notice may not be delayed on grounds that the total number of affected residents is not yet known. Ch. 93H § 3A (added by St. 2018, c. 444, signed Jan 2019, eff. Apr 2019) mandates free credit monitoring for at least 18 months when SSN is involved — 42 months if the breached entity is a consumer reporting agency; entity must certify monitoring compliance to AG/OCABR and cannot condition it on waiving the private right of action. Regs at 201 CMR 17.00 impose separate security duties. All values independently verified.

Maryland Personal Information Protection Act (Com. Law §§ 14-3501 to 14-3508). 2022 HB 962 (eff. 10/1/2022) made the 45 days run from discovery/notification of the breach (not from conclusion of investigation) and cut service-provider notice to owners to 10 days — verified. AG must be notified PRIOR to individual notices, for every covered breach (threshold 1). 2022 amendments also added genetic data. Maryland's 2024 Online Data Privacy Act (MODPA) is a separate law and does not replace § 14-3504.

Notice of Risk to Personal Data Act (10 M.R.S. §§ 1346–1350-B). 30-day cap verified — added by PL 2019, ch. 512 (which also extended coverage to municipalities/school administrative units); runs from when the entity becomes aware of the breach and identifies its scope. Entities must notify the AG or, if regulated, the appropriate regulators within the Dept. of Professional and Financial Regulation — required for every covered breach (threshold 1). CRA notice if >1,000 notified. Law-enforcement delay: notice due within 7 business days after law enforcement determines notification will not compromise the investigation. Official URL confirmed live.

Identity Theft Protection Act (2004 PA 452). Notice 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. No AG/agency notice requirement under current law (AG has enforcement authority; civil fines up to $250/failure, $750,000 aggregate per breach); CRA notice if >1,000 residents notified. LIVE LEGISLATIVE RISK: SB 360 (2025–2026 session) — which amends MCL 445.63/445.72/445.72b, adds new sections, and would expand breach duties — PASSED THE SENATE in 2025 and was pending in House Government Operations as of late 2025; no Public Act found as of Aug 2026, but the session runs through Dec 2026. Re-verify enactment status before each republication; if enacted, deadline and AG-notice fields will likely change.

'Most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. No AG/agency notice requirement in § 325E.61 (AG enforces via § 8.31); must notify nationwide CRAs within 48 hours if >500 persons are notified at one time. Separate rules apply to government entities (Minn. Stat. § 13.055). The Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act (ch. 325O, eff. July 31, 2025) is a separate privacy law and does not alter this breach-notice statute.

VERIFIED against Missouri Revisor text. Individual notice 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count, so deadline is null. AG and nationwide CRAs must be notified when notice is given to MORE THAN 1,000 consumers at one time, so the at-or-above threshold is correctly encoded as 1001 (secondary charts often round to 1,000). AG has exclusive enforcement (civil penalty up to $150,000 per breach); no private right of action. No mandated credit monitoring.

Notice 'without unreasonable delay' after completing investigation — no fixed day count. NO AG notice requirement as of Aug 2026 — verified: SB2528 (2022), HB1625 (2024), and SB2046 (2025, died in committee 2/4/2025) all failed; the 2026 SB2046 is an UNRELATED name/likeness/voice bill (died 3/3/2026), and no 2026 refile of the AG-notice amendment was found. The only enacted 2026 MS cyber law, HB 1220 (eff. 7/1/2026), is an insurance-code cybersecurity safe harbor amending § 83-5-803 — it does not touch § 75-24-29. CAUTION: some AI-generated secondary sites present the failed '>100 affected → AG notice' provision as current law; disregard them. Violations are unfair trade practices enforced by the AG; no private right of action. Confidence medium due to reliance on mirror text and conflicting secondary sources. URL is the official Mississippi Legislature gateway: the official Mississippi Code is Lexis-hosted public access reachable from legislature.ms.gov and sos.ms.gov with no stable per-section deep link (re-confirmed by live search 2026-08-02); navigate to Miss. Code Ann. § 75-24-29. Third-party mirrors (Justia/FindLaw) exist but are not cited.

VERIFIED against MCA text on mca.legmt.gov (current official legislature site). Individual notice 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. An electronic copy of the notification plus date/method of distribution must be submitted SIMULTANEOUSLY to the AG's Consumer Protection Office for every covered breach (2015 amendment) — threshold = 1. Montana DOJ accepts submissions by email (contactocp@mt.gov). The 2023 Montana Consumer Data Privacy Act did not replace this breach statute. No mandated credit monitoring.

Verified. Identity Theft Protection Act (G.S. 75-61 to 75-66). Individual notice 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. Every breach requiring consumer notice must also be reported to the Consumer Protection Division of the NC AG's Office (§ 75-65(e1)), so AG threshold = 1. SSN covered via 'identifying information' in § 75-61(10) cross-referencing G.S. 14-113.20(b). CRA notice additionally required at >1,000 notified.

Verified. Individual notice 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. AG notice required for any breach that 'exceeds two hundred fifty individuals,' i.e., 251+ under this schema's at/above convention. Statutory wording counts 'individuals' (arguably total, not only ND residents) — flag retained for manual read. Official ND Century Code published as chapter PDFs on ndlegis.gov.

VERIFIED against nebraskalegislature.gov text; section heading itself includes 'notice to Attorney General.' Financial Data Protection and Consumer Notification of Data Security Breach Act (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 87-801 to 87-807). Individual notice 'as soon as possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. AG must be notified NOT LATER THAN the time notice is provided to residents, for every covered breach (2016 LB 835) — threshold = 1. No mandated credit monitoring.

VERIFIED against gc.nh.gov text (General Court site migrated from gencourt.state.nh.us). Statutory standard is notice 'as soon as possible' after determining misuse occurred or is reasonably likely (author's note said 'as quickly as possible' — corrected wording; no field impact, deadline remains null). Every covered breach must be reported to the NH AG (anticipated notice date and approximate number of NH residents), EXCEPT persons in trade/commerce subject to RSA 358-A:3, I, who instead notify their primary regulator — threshold = 1. CRA notice required if more than 1,000 residents notified. No mandated credit monitoring.

VERIFIED substantively: individual notice 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. The Division of State Police (Dept. of Law and Public Safety, under the AG) must be notified IN ADVANCE of customer disclosure for every covered breach — threshold = 1 (designated agency is State Police, not the AG directly). CRA notice if more than 1,000 customers. 2019 amendment (eff. Sept. 1, 2019) added online account credentials as a trigger. Confidence stays medium solely because NJ's official statute portal (njleg.state.nj.us) lacks stable section-level deep links — URL is the Legislature's statute search page; navigate to Title 56, § 56:8-163. Manual link re-verification recommended.

VERIFIED: Data Breach Notification Act, N.M. Stat. Ann. §§ 57-12C-1 to -12 (2017). Individual notice in the most expedient time possible, no later than 45 calendar days after discovery (risk-of-harm exception applies). AG and CRA notice within 45 days when notification goes to MORE THAN 1,000 NM residents from a single breach (§ 57-12C-10) — 1001 is the correct at-or-above encoding. No mandated credit monitoring. Confidence medium solely because of the URL: NMOneSource (NM Compilation Commission) is the official publisher but reliable section-level deep links are unavailable — navigate to NMSA ch. 57, art. 12C. All substantive values independently confirmed.

VERIFIED: NRS 603A.220 requires individual notice 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count — and contains NO mandatory AG/state-agency notice (null); the AG's office only invites voluntary submissions. CRA notice required if more than 1,000 persons are notified at one time (§ 603A.220(6)). Sector-specific exception noted by author (2023 SB 355, licensed lenders under NRS ch. 675, AG notice within 30 days when >500 residents affected) could not be independently re-verified in this pass — treat that note as needing manual confirmation; it does not affect this general-statute row. URL is the official chapter page; deep-link anchor #NRS603ASec220.

VERIFIED: December 2024 amendment (effective Dec. 21, 2024) replaced the open-ended 'most expedient time possible' standard with a fixed 30-day deadline for notifying affected individuals after discovery, and removed the scope-determination/system-restoration delay allowance. Sources conflict on the signing date (Dec. 21 vs. Dec. 24, 2024) — effective date Dec. 21, 2024 is what matters; author's 'signed Dec. 21' should read 'effective Dec. 21.' AG, Dept. of State, and Division of State Police must be notified whenever any NY residents are notified (threshold = 1); the amendment added NYDFS to the regulator-notice list (eff. Mar. 21, 2025) and added medical/health-insurance data to 'private information.' CRA notice if more than 5,000 residents notified. SHIELD Act security-program duties are in companion § 899-bb. No mandated credit monitoring.

Verified. Notice 'in the most expedient time possible but not later than forty-five days' after discovery or notification of the breach (§ 1349.19(B)(2)). No AG or state-agency notification requirement in the statute — only CRA notice when >1,000 residents affected — hence null (Ohio is one of the few states without a regulator-notice duty). ORC 1347.12 covers state agencies; ORC 1354 (Data Protection Act) is a separate safe harbor, not a notice duty.

Security Breach Notification Act, 24 O.S. §§ 161-166, as amended by SB 626 (2025), effective Jan. 1, 2026. Individual notice remains 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. Fact-check confirmed against the enrolled bill (oklegislature.gov SB626 ENR): AG notice required when a breach affects 500 OR MORE OK residents (i.e., threshold 500, not 501), due within 60 days; SB 626 amends existing §§ 162, 163, 164, 165, and 166 (no new section), adds biometric/electronic-identifier elements, and creates a reasonable-safeguards affirmative defense ($75,000 penalty cap if safeguards lacking but notice timely; $150,000 if both lacking). Confidence stays medium only because the URL is the official OSCN Title 24 table-of-contents rather than a section deep-link, and the post-amendment codified text on OSCN should be spot-checked for the AG-notice subsection placement within § 163.

Verified. Oregon Consumer Information Protection Act (ORS 646A.600-646A.628). Notice 'in the most expeditious manner possible, without unreasonable delay, but not later than 45 days' after discovery/notification. AG notice when the number of consumers to be notified 'exceeds 250,' i.e., 251+. Monitoring not mandated, but if offered it may not be conditioned on providing a credit/debit card number. URL is the official ORS chapter 646A page (whole chapter; no per-section official page).

Verified. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act (Act 94 of 2005, 73 P.S. §§ 2301-2330). Private-entity individual notice 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count (state agencies/contractors: 7 business days under Act 151 of 2020; Commonwealth agencies notify AG within 3 business days). Act 33 of 2024 (SB 824, signed June 28, 2024 — official act title 'Act of Jun. 28, 2024, P.L. 427, No. 33'; some secondary sources misstate July — effective Sept. 26, 2024): AG notice when MORE THAN 500 PA residents affected (501+); free independent credit report plus 12 months of free credit monitoring required when the breach involves SSN, driver's license/state ID number, or bank account number. '73 P.S.' is Purdon's (unofficial) numbering — official source is the session law on legis.state.pa.us; Act 33 text: https://www.legis.state.pa.us/WU01/LI/LI/US/HTM/2024/0/0033..HTM.

Verified. Identity Theft Protection Act of 2015 (chapter 11-49.3). Notice 'in the most expedient time possible but no later than forty-five (45) calendar days after confirmation of the breach and the ability to ascertain the information required' — trigger is confirmation, not discovery. AG (and major CRAs) notified when more than 500 RI residents are to be notified, i.e., 501+. The 2024 RI Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act (eff. Jan. 1, 2026) is a comprehensive privacy law and does not replace this breach statute.

Verified. Individual notice 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. Report goes to the Consumer Protection Division of the SC Department of Consumer Affairs (not the AG) plus nationwide CRAs when notice is provided to more than 1,000 persons at one time, i.e., 1,001+ (§ 39-1-90(K)); recorded per the field's 'AG or designated state agency' definition. Official URL is the scstatehouse.gov Title 39, Chapter 1 page (no per-section official page). Insurance licensees separately covered by the SC Insurance Data Security Act (§ 38-99-10 et seq., 72-hour Director notice) — out of scope.

Verified: consumer notice within 60 days of discovery/notification (SDCL 22-40-20, enacted 2018 SB 62; scheme is §§ 22-40-19 to -26, SSN in § 22-40-19 definitions). AG disclosure required when a breach 'exceeds 250 residents' — 251 is the correct at/above encoding; many secondary charts loosely say '250.' Harm-based exemption from consumer notice requires prior notice to the AG. Official SD Legislature permalink confirmed to resolve to § 22-40-20. No mandated monitoring.

Verified: disclosure immediately but no later than 45 days from discovery/notification (2016 amendment); no AG/state-agency notice requirement; nationwide consumer reporting agencies notified if more than 1,000 persons notified at once. Encryption safe harbor lost if the key was also acquired. URL caveat stands: Tennessee's official free code is the LexisNexis hot-topics portal (no state-hosted code site, no deep links) — navigate to Title 47, Ch. 18, Part 21.

Verified: individuals notified without unreasonable delay and not later than 60 days after determining a breach occurred (HB 4390, 2019). AG notice when 250 or more Texas residents affected, not later than 30 days after determination (SB 768, 2023, eff. 9/1/2023, shortened from 60), submitted electronically via the AG's form; AG publishes a public breach list (HB 3746, 2021). Trigger is 'sensitive personal information' including name + SSN. No mandated monitoring.

Verified: Protection of Personal Information Act; consumer notice in most expedient time possible without unreasonable delay — no fixed day count (null is correct). Misuse/likely-misuse investigation trigger. SB 127 (2023, eff. May 2, 2023) requires notice to both the AG and the Utah Cyber Center when misuse of personal information of 500 or more Utah residents has occurred or is reasonably likely; consumer reporting agencies at 1,000 or more. SSN in § 13-44-102 definitions. URL follows le.utah.gov's standard xcode pattern but the site blocks automated fetches — spot-check the link manually.

Verified: notice to the Office of the Attorney General and affected residents 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count (null correct); AG notice applies to every covered breach (threshold 1). Harm trigger: unencrypted/unredacted personal info accessed and acquired that causes or is reasonably believed will cause identity theft or other fraud. Consumer reporting agencies notified if more than 1,000 residents notified. Separate payroll/withholding-data duty for employers and payroll providers (AG notice even absent consumer notice); medical information covered by § 32.1-127.1:05. No mandated monitoring.

Verified: Security Breach Notice Act (9 V.S.A. § 2435; SSN in § 2430 definitions). Consumers: most expedient time possible, not later than 45 days after discovery/notification. Regulator notice for every covered breach (threshold 1): preliminary AG notice within 14 business days of discovery plus a copy of the consumer notice when sent; sworn-affirmation option modifies the date-of-breach element (AG's current 14-day affirmation form confirmed live). DFR-regulated entities notify DFR instead of the AG. Login-credential-only breaches have alternate notice rules. No mandated monitoring.

Verified: per HB 1071 (2019, eff. 3/1/2020) consumer notice no more than 30 calendar days after discovery; AG notice no more than 30 days after discovery when notice to 'more than 500' Washington residents is required — 501 is the correct at/above encoding (many summaries round to 500). Definitions, including SSN and expanded elements (full DOB, biometrics, health/medical insurance info, student/military/passport IDs, username-or-email + password), sit in RCW 19.255.005. Parallel agency provision at RCW 42.56.590. Private right of action exists. No mandated monitoring.

Verified: notice 'within a reasonable time,' not to exceed 45 days after the entity learns of the acquisition; personal information includes name + SSN. No AG/state-agency notice requirement; consumer reporting agencies notified if 1,000 or more individuals must be notified from a single incident. Notice not required if the acquisition creates no material risk of identity theft or fraud. No private right of action; forfeitures up to $10,000 per violation. Official docs.legis.wisconsin.gov URL confirmed. No mandated monitoring.

Verified: WV Consumer Credit and Protection Act, art. 2A (§§ 46A-2A-101 to -105; SSN in § 46A-2A-101 definitions). Resident notice 'without unreasonable delay' — no fixed day count. No AG/state-agency notice requirement found, and no 2024-2025 amendment adding one; consumer reporting agencies notified if more than 1,000 persons notified. Harm trigger: unauthorized access + acquisition reasonably believed to cause identity theft or other fraud. AG has exclusive enforcement (civil penalties capped at $150,000 per breach for repeated willful violations). Official code.wvlegislature.gov URL confirmed. No mandated monitoring.

Verified substantively: notice to affected persons 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' after an investigation determines misuse occurred or is reasonably likely — no fixed day count. No AG/state-agency notice requirement (AG has enforcement authority only); no mandated monitoring. Definitions in § 40-12-501 include SSN plus 2015-added elements (biometric data, username/email + password, etc.). Confidence stays medium solely for the URL: Wyoming publishes statutes only as title-level PDF/Word downloads with no section-level pages, so the Title 40 PDF link follows wyoleg.gov's standard pattern and should be manually re-verified.
